WEEK 31 ERP PROGRAMME STEERING — NOTES
Date: 2026-07-28 | Chair: Priya Nair | Location: Board Room 3 / Teams

Priya Nair opened the meeting and immediately flagged that the data profiling results received this morning represent a material change to programme status.

[AISHA KAMARA]: The BODS profiling job completed overnight. I’ve run full validation today and confirmed 43,847 records in GL_ACCOUNTS with at least one null mandatory field. This affects approximately 31% of the total GL account master dataset. The fields impacted are cost_centre (38,211 nulls), profit_centre (41,903 nulls), and account_type (12,540 nulls). Company codes GBUK and DEFRANKFURT are the most affected. My working hypothesis is that these records were migrated from a pre-ECC legacy system around 2014 and the mandatory fields were not populated at that time.

[MARCUS CHEN]: This is consistent with what I know about those two company codes. They were brought onto ECC in a rush cut-over in 2014 and the data quality controls were not as mature as they are now. The question is: can we infer the correct values from the account group hierarchy, or does Finance need to manually review all 44k records?

[LIN WEI]: I am not prepared to allow blanket default injection without review. These are general ledger accounts. An incorrect cost centre mapping will corrupt our management accounts from day one of go-live. We need a proper audit.

[PRIYA NAIR]: Agreed. I’m formally classifying the data migration workstream as RED. I will convene an emergency committee this week. Robert, I need your backing for contingency resource spend if we need external consultants.

[ROBERT CHANG]: Approved. Up to £75k without further escalation. Get this sorted, Priya. And please pull the lessons-learned from the 2021 payroll migration — we had similar issues then and I don’t want to relearn the same lessons.

Meeting closed at 15:45.

EMERGENCY DATA QUALITY COMMITTEE — SESSION 1
Date: 2026-07-30 | Chair: Priya Nair | Location: Teams call

[PRIYA NAIR]: Thank you all for joining at short notice. The purpose of this committee is to agree the remediation approach for the GL_ACCOUNTS data quality issue, manage the audit programme, and protect the ERP go-live timeline as much as possible.

[MARCUS CHEN]: I’ve prepared three options and circulated them in advance. Let me walk through them quickly. Option A is exclusion of null records from the initial go-live — clean but creates a two-wave migration and parallel system operation. Option B is intelligent default mapping driven by BODS rules derived from the account group hierarchy, with Finance validating each mapping. Option C is bulk default injection without Finance review — I’m listing it for completeness but I’m not recommending it.

[LIN WEI]: Option C is off the table. I said that in my email and I mean it. The risk to the statutory accounts is too high. Option A is operationally very disruptive — my team cannot work across two systems during year-end.

[EMMA TRENT]: Option B is workable. The proposed default mapping workbook format is clear. My four analysts can get through the 9,600 manual records in about two weeks if we prioritise it.

[AISHA KAMARA]: The good news is that Marcus’s BODS logic covers about 78% of records with high confidence — around 34,000 records. So the Finance manual review workload is about 9,600 records, not 44k. That’s manageable.

[PRIYA NAIR]: Decision taken: we proceed with Option B. Marcus and Aisha, I need the workbook and transformation rules ready for Finance by 7 August. Emma, can you confirm your team starts review on 10 August?

[EMMA TRENT]: Confirmed.

[PRIYA NAIR]: Revised migration design target is 28 August, subject to Finance sign-off completing by 21 August. I’ll communicate this to steering. Next committee session: Thursday 6 August.

SAP parallel run (legacy ECC and S/4HANA operating simultaneously for at least one full month-end cycle) is mandatory before go-live approval.
Data migration must achieve 100% reconciliation of opening GL balances (within agreed tolerance of 0.01%) before Finance sign-off on go-live.
Lin Wei to brief the CFO by 5 August with a Finance Continuity Risk Summary, co-authored with Priya Nair.

FINANCE CONTINUITY RISK REVIEW
Date: 2026-08-01 | Chair: Lin Wei | Location: Finance Committee Room

[LIN WEI]: I called this meeting because I need the programme to understand our constraints very precisely. The ERP programme is important, but it cannot break Finance operations during the most critical period of our year. Let me state the non-negotiables.

[DAVID PARK]: From a reporting perspective, we are completely locked down from 1 November. That’s when we begin the year-end accruals process. By mid-November we are running the IFRS consolidation pack. December is statutory accounts and tax. Any system instability in that window is catastrophic.

[LIN WEI]: Exactly. So my position is: if we are not in a stable, hypercare-complete state by 1 October 2026, the go-live must be deferred to March 2027. That is a binary decision.

[PRIYA NAIR]: I understand and I will register that as a hard constraint. The current revised timeline, assuming the GL_ACCOUNTS remediation completes by 21 August, gives us a migration design sign-off in late August, ETL development through September-October, integration testing in November, and Finance UAT in December-January. That timetable does not hit a 1 October go-live. We are almost certainly looking at March 2027 unless we can significantly compress later phases.

[LIN WEI]: Then we need to plan for March 2027 and ensure the year-end is protected regardless. Emma, David — I need a manual contingency plan for November and December so that if something unexpected happens with the ERP, Finance can still close the books.

[EMMA TRENT]: Understood. We still have the old month-end runbooks from ECC. I’ll update them and have a draft by 21 August.

[AISHA KAMARA]: One thing I want to confirm: do you require a full parallel run, and if so, for how long?

[LIN WEI]: Minimum one full month-end cycle. Non-negotiable. If we can do two cycles, even better.

[PRIYA NAIR]: I’ll build that into the revised programme plan. Thank you, Lin. I’ll co-author the CFO briefing with you — can we get together Thursday morning?

[LIN WEI]: Thursday works. Let’s keep it factual and honest about the risks.
